name: Yellow curry chicken & sweet potato tray bake (עוף בקארי צהוב ובטטות בתבנית אחת)

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption) — part of a 'good to pack for work' meal-prep series
source.notes: One-tray meal: chicken fillet and cubed sweet potato marinated in yellow curry paste + coconut milk + cornstarch + baking soda, broiled on the top rack ~15 min. Posted as a work-lunch meal-prep dish meant to reheat well. Serves well as 4 portions given 1 kg chicken + 2 sweet potatoes. SODIUM IS A ROUGH ESTIMATE AND LIKELY HIGH: the marinade includes curry paste, 1 tsp added salt, AND ½ tbsp baking soda (not rinsed off per the method), which stacks up fast — flagged clearly in the analysis as the dish's main weak point. Coconut liquid (נוזל קוקוס) taken as standard canned coconut milk. Rice ('to serve') not quantified, excluded from macros. Estimate.

steps: Preheat the oven to 300 °C on top broil.
Whisk the curry paste, coconut milk, oil, salt, cornstarch and baking soda (and ginger, if using) into a smooth marinade.
Add the chicken and coat well; let it sit 15–30 min.
Cut the sweet potatoes into thin-ish cubes or rounds so they cook at the same rate as the chicken.
Arrange the chicken on a parchment-lined tray.
Toss the sweet potato in the leftover marinade and arrange around the chicken.
Broil on the top rack, close to the element, ~15 min (varies by oven) until the chicken is nicely browned and the sweet potato is soft and browned.
Finish with chopped cilantro and a squeeze of lime or lemon. Serve with rice to soak up the pan juices.

batch_totals.note: Whole tray (4 servings), excl. rice. VERY high sodium estimate (~5,185 mg batch) — three separate sodium sources stack up: 1 tsp added salt, the curry paste, and the baking soda (which isn't rinsed off in this method, unlike other velveting recipes in this library). Worth moderating if making this a regular lunch.

him.verdict: Excellent protein density — ~55.8 g protein for 458 kcal (~12.2 g protein per 100 kcal, one of the best in your library), from a full kilo of chicken breast split 4 ways. Sweet potato adds real vitamin A and some fiber. The clear weak point is sodium: between the added salt, the curry paste, and un-rinsed baking soda, this comes out very high (~1,300 mg/serving by estimate) — worth real moderation if this becomes a weekly meal-prep staple, since it's meant to be eaten several days in a row.
flags: ~55.8 g protein / 458 kcal (~12.2 g protein per 100 kcal — excellent)
very high sodium estimate (~1,300 mg/serving) — salt + curry paste + baking soda all stack up
good vitamin A + some fiber from sweet potato
broiled, not fried — no deep-fry oil to add
meal-prep friendly (the point of the recipe) but the sodium load compounds over several servings/days
suggested_mods: Drop the added 1 tsp salt entirely — the curry paste alone brings real sodium, and this is the easiest cut
Use low-sodium curry paste if your brand offers one, or use a bit less of it
Scale back the baking soda or, if you want to keep using a full ½ tbsp for tenderizing, consider rinsing it off before the marinade step (as done elsewhere in this library) rather than leaving it in
Great dish for the stated use-case (reheats well); just watch total daily sodium on days you eat it

her_preconception.verdict: Good protein and a real vitamin-A contribution from the sweet potato, fully cooked chicken — no safety flags. The sodium load is the one thing worth moderating in pregnancy more broadly; otherwise this is a fine, filling dish. Not a folate or choline standout on its own.
prenatal_highlights: protein (chicken); vitamin A + some fiber (sweet potato)
suggested_mods: Same sodium-reduction mods as for him — worth it in pregnancy generally
Pair with a green veg side for folate, which this dish doesn't otherwise provide

cooking_guide: Whisk the marinade smooth before adding the chicken — curry paste can clump, so break it up against the side of the bowl first.
Don't skip the marinating time (15–30 min) — the baking soda and cornstarch are doing real tenderizing and coating work in that window.
Cut the sweet potato pieces genuinely thin (cubes or rounds) — the recipe is time-constrained by the chicken's broil time, so thick pieces simply won't cook through in ~15 min under a broiler.
Arrange everything in a single layer, not piled up — crowding blocks the broiler's direct heat and you lose the browning that makes this dish work.
Broil close to the top element and watch it — broilers vary a lot between ovens, and this can go from perfectly charred to burnt quickly.
The cilantro and citrus at the end aren't optional garnish here — the acidity cuts through the rich coconut-curry marinade and brightens the whole dish.
Tip: if sodium is a concern, skip the added salt and taste the marinade before considering any more — the curry paste alone is usually salty enough.
